title: Shift Solenoid A
plain: There's a problem with shift solenoid A, one of the electric valves the computer uses to change gears.
symptoms: Transmission stuck in one gear or skipping gears
Worse fuel economy or high RPM at highway speed

causes.name: Damaged wiring or connector (often the internal harness)
Sticking valve or debris in the valve body

checks: Check fluid level and condition
Measure the solenoid resistance through the transmission connector
Command the solenoid on and off with a scanner and watch for a gear change
fix: Usually a new shift solenoid (on many models sold as a solenoid pack) or a wiring repair; check the fluid first.

title: Shift Solenoid A Performance or Stuck Off
plain: Shift solenoid A isn't doing what the computer commands, or seems stuck off, so the transmission may not make certain shifts.
symptoms: Transmission stuck in one gear or skipping gears

causes.name: Damaged wiring or connector (often the internal harness)

checks: Check fluid level and condition
Measure the solenoid resistance through the transmission connector
Command the solenoid on and off with a scanner and watch for a gear change
fix: Usually a new shift solenoid (on many models sold as a solenoid pack) or a wiring repair; check the fluid first.

title: Shift Solenoid A Stuck On
plain: Shift solenoid A appears stuck on, so the transmission may stay in or jump to the wrong gear.
symptoms: Transmission stuck in one gear or skipping gears

Measure the solenoid resistance through the transmission connector
Command the solenoid on and off with a scanner and watch for a gear change
fix: Usually a new shift solenoid (on many models sold as a solenoid pack) or a wiring repair; check the fluid first.

title: Gear 7 Incorrect Ratio
plain: The computer compared the speeds going into and out of the transmission and found they don't match what seventh gear should give, which usually means something is slipping.
symptoms: Slipping or flaring RPM in the higher gears
Transmission may go into limp mode

causes.name: Low, burnt or wrong transmission fluid
Faulty shift or pressure control solenoid

checks: Check fluid level and condition
Check for solenoid or speed sensor codes and fix those first
fix: Check and correct the fluid first. If solenoids and sensors test good, the transmission usually needs internal repair.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid B
plain: There's a problem with the second pressure control solenoid, which helps set the hydraulic pressure the transmission uses to apply its clutches.

causes.name: Damaged wiring or connector (often the internal harness)

checks: Check fluid level and condition
Measure the solenoid resistance through the transmission connector
Check line pressure with a gauge if shifting is harsh or soft
fix: Usually a new pressure control solenoid (on some models part of the solenoid pack or valve body) or a wiring repair; check the fluid first.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Performance or Stuck Off
plain: The second pressure control solenoid isn't changing pressure the way the computer commands, or seems stuck off, often causing harsh or slipping shifts.

causes.name: Damaged wiring or connector (often the internal harness)
Sticking valve in the valve body

checks: Check fluid level and condition
Measure the solenoid resistance through the transmission connector
Check line pressure with a gauge if shifting is harsh or soft
fix: Usually a new pressure control solenoid (on some models part of the solenoid pack or valve body) or a wiring repair; check the fluid first.

title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Stuck On
plain: The second pressure control solenoid appears stuck on, so transmission pressure isn't being controlled properly.

causes.name: Damaged wiring or connector (often the internal harness)

checks: Check fluid level and condition
Measure the solenoid resistance through the transmission connector
Check line pressure with a gauge if shifting is harsh or soft
fix: Usually a new pressure control solenoid (on some models part of the solenoid pack or valve body) or a wiring repair; check the fluid first.
